G4700.def:
σποδός, -oῦ, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for אֵפֶר ;] 
ashes: Hébreux 9:13; ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σ. (Ésaïe 58:5, Jean 3:6, Dan LXX 9:3, al.), Matthieu 11:21, Luc 10:13.†

G4701.def:
σπορά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(σπείρω), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:29 (זָרַע), 1Ma.10:30 * ;] 
__1. a sowing. 
__2. seedtime. 
__3. seed sown (of human offspring, Soph., Tr., 316, 420): 1 Pierre 1:23 
(cf. σπέρμα, and see Milligan, NTD, 105 f.).†

G4702.def:
σπόριμος, -ον
(σπείρω) [in LXX: Genèse 1:29, Lévitique 11:37 (זָרַע), Sir 40:22 א1 * ;] 
fit for sowing, sown; as subst., τὰ σ., corn-fields: Matthieu 12:1, Marc 2:23, Luc 6:1.†

G4703.def:
σπόρος, -ου, ὁ
(σπείρω), [in LXX chiefly for זֶרַע ;] 
= σπορά, 
__1. sowing or seedtime. 
__2. seed sown (so usually in late Gk.): Marc 4:26-27, Luc 8:5, 11, 2 Corinthiens 9:10 a (LTr.); metaphorically, of almsgiving, 2 Corinthiens 9:10 b.†

G4704.def:
σπουδάζω
(σπουδή), [in LXX chiefly for בָּהַל ;] 
to make haste; hence, to be zealous or eager, to give diligence: with inf. (see M, Pr., 205 f.), Galates 2:10, Éphésiens 4:3, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:17, 2 Timothée 2:15 4:9 4:21, Tite 3:12, Hébreux 4:11, 2 Pierre 1:10 3:14; with accusative and inf. (on this construction see Mayor in l; MM, xxiii), 2 Pierre 1:15 (for other constructions see LS, see word).†

G4705.def:
σπουδαῖος, -α, -ον
(σπουδή), [in LXX: Eze.41:25 * ;] 
in haste; hence, zealous, eager, diligent, earnest: before ἐν, 2 Corinthiens 8:22; compar., -οτεροσς 2 Corinthiens 8:17 (here in superl. sense, see Bl., § 44, 3) 2 Corinthiens 8:22.†

G4708.def:
earnestly, zealously, with vigor; (compar.) all the more eager, with special urgency eagerly 
earnestly, eagerly, diligently, Lk. 7:4; 2Tim. 1:17; Tit. 3:13; comparative σπουδαιοτέρως, more earnestly, with special urgency, Phil. 2:28

G4709.def:
σπουδαίως
adv. (σπουδαῖος), [in LXX: Wis.2:6 * ;] 
__1. with haste or zeal, i.e. earnestly, zealously, diligently: Luc 7:4, 2 Timothée 1:17, Tite 3:13; compar., -οτέρως, Philippiens 2:28 (RV, Lft., Weymouth, al., but see infr.) 
__2. hastily, speedily: compar., -οτέρως, Philippiens 2:28 (Thayer, Zorell, see word; ICC, in l, al., but see supr.).†

G4710.def:
σπουδή, -ῆς, ἡ
(σπεύδω), [in LXX chiefly for בָּהַל, its parts and derivatives ;] 
__1. haste, speed: μετὰ σ. (Wis.19:2), Marc 6:25, Luc 1:39. 
__2. zeal, diligence, earnestness: Romains 12:11, 2 Corinthiens 7:11-12 8:7-8; ἐν σ., Romains 12:8 (see M, Pr, 104); before ὑπέρ, 2 Corinthiens 8:16; σπουδὴν ἐνδείκνυσθαι, Hébreux 6:11; σ. παρεισφέρειν, 2 Pierre 1:5; πᾶσαν σ. ποιεῖσθαι, Ju 3 (see MM, xxiii; M, Pr., 214; Deiss., BS, 361, 364).†

G4711.def:
σφυρίς (T, Rec. σπυρίς, see WH, App., 148; 131., § 6, 7), -ίδος, ἡ, 
a flexible mat-basket for carrying provisions: Matthieu 15:37 16:10, Marc 8:8, 20 Actes 9:25 (see: κόφινος).†

G4712.def:
στάδιον, -ου, τό pl., στάδια (Jean 6:19, T), and metapl., στάδιοι (see B1., 9, 1), 
[in LXX: Dan LXX 4:9, Sus 1:37, 2Ma.11:5 2Mac 12:9 ff. * ;] 
a stadium, i.e. 
__1. a measure of length = 600 Greek feet or 1⁄8 of a Roman mile Matthieu 14:24 (Rec., WH, txt., R, mg.), Luc 24:13, Jean 6:19 11:18, Apocalypse 14:20 21:16, and, this being the length of the Olympic course, 
__2. a race-course: 1 Corinthiens 9:24.†

G4713.def:
στάρνος, -ου (ὁ and), ἡ 
[in LXX: Exode 16:33 (צִנְצֶנֶת), 3Ki.12:24 14:3 (בַּקְבֻּק), Dan LXX Bel, 1:32 * ;] 
prop., an earthen jar for racking off wine, hence, generally, a jar: Hébreux 9:4.†

G4714.def:
στάσις, -εως, ἡ
(ἵστημι), [in LXX chiefly for עָמַד, its parts and derivatives, also for רִיב (Pr 1714), etc. (see Deiss., BS, 158 f.) ;] 
__1. a standing, place, status: σ. ἔχειν (Polyb., v, 5, 3; and cf. Lat. locum habere), Hébreux 9:8. 
__2. insurrection, sedition: Marc 15:7, Luc 23:19, 25, Actes 19:40 24:5. 
__3. In poets and late prose, strife, dissension (cf. MM, xxiii) Actes 15:2 23:7, 10.†

G4716.def:
σταυρός, -oῦ, ὁ 
__1. an upright pale or stake (Hom., Hdt., Thuc., al.) 
__2. In late writers (Diod., Plut., al.) of the Roman instrument of crucifixion, the Cross: of the Cross on which Christ suffered, Matthieu 27:32, 40 27:42, Marc 15:21, 30 15:32, Luc 23:26, Jean 19:17, 19 19:25, 31, Colossiens 2:14, Hébreux 12:2; θάνατος σταυροῦ, Philippiens 2:8; τ. αἷμα τοῦ σ., Colossiens 1:20. Metaphorical, in proverbial sayings: αἴρειν (λαμβάνειν, βαστάζειν) τὸν σ., Matthieu 10:38 16:24, Marc 8:34 10:21, 15:21, Luc 9:23 14:27 (for an interesting ex. of metaphorically use in π., see MM, xxiii) By meton., for Christ's death on the Cross: 1 Corinthiens 1:17, Galates 5:11 6:12, 14, Éphésiens 2:16, Philippiens 3:18; ὁ λόγος ὁ τοῦ σ., 1 Corinthiens 1:18.†

G4717.def:
σταυρόω, -ῶ
(σταυρός), [in LXX: Esther 7:9 (תָּלָה), Esther 8:13 * ;] 
__1. to fence with pales, impalisade (Thuc.). 
__2. In late writers (Polyb., FlJ; but ἀνασταυρόω is more common) to crucify: with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 20:19 23:34 26:2 27:22 ff. Matthieu 28:5, Marc 15:16 ff. Marc 16:6, Luc 23:21, 23 23:33 24:7, 20, Jean 19:6 ff., Actes 2:36 4:10, 1 Corinthiens 1:13 1:23 2:2 2:8, 2 Corinthiens 13:4, Galates 3:1, Apocalypse 11:8; metaphorically, Galates 5:24 6:14.†

G4718.def:
σταφυλή, -ῆς, ἡ 
[in LXX for עֵנָב ;] 
a bunch of grapes: Matthieu 7:16, Luc 6:44, Apocalypse 14:18. "σ. is properly the ripe grape-cluster as opposite to ὄμφαξ, cf. Genèse 40:10, Job 15:33; as contrasted with βότρυς, it describes the grapes rather than the cluster on which they grow" (Swete, Apoc., 187 f.).†

G4719.def:
στάχυς, -υος, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for שִׁבֹּל ;] 
an ear of corn: Matthieu 12:1, Marc 2:23 4:28, Luc 6:1.†

G4720.def:
Στάχυς, -υος, ὁ 
Stachys: Romains 16:9 (see Lft., Phi., 174; MM, xxiii).†

G4721.def:
στέγη, -ης, ἡ
(στέγω) [in LXX: Genèse 8:13 (מְכַסֶּה), etc. ;] 
a roof: Marc 2:4; of entering a house, εἰσέρχεσθαι ὑπὸ τὴν σ., Matthieu 8:8, Luc 7:6 (cf. MM, xxiii).†

G4722.def:
στέγω
(cf. Lat. tego), [in LXX: Sir.8:17 * ;] 
__1. prop., to cover closely, to protect by covering, esp. to keep water in or out (Soph., Plat., al.). 
__2. to cover, keep secret, conceal (Sir, l.with, Polyb., al.): 1 Corinthiens 13:7, R, mg. 
__3. By covering to ward of, bear up under, endure (for exx., see, Lft., Notes, 40; M, Th., 36): 1 Corinthiens 9:12 13:7, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:1 3:5.†

G4723.def:
στεῖρος, -ον also -α, -ον, 
[in LXX for עָקָר ;] 
barren: of a woman, Luc 1:7, 36 23:29, Galates 4:27" (LXX) .†

G4724.def:
στέλλω 
[in LXX (mid.): Malachie 2:5 (חָתַת ni.), Proverbes 31:24 (26), Wis.7:14 14:1, 2Ma.5:1, 3Ma.1:19 3Mac 4:11 * ;] 
__1. prop., to set, place, arrange, fit out; hence, mid., to set oneself for, prepare (Wis, xi Mac, ll. with). 
__2. to bring together, gather up (in Hom. of furling sails), hence to restrain, check; mid., to restrain or withdraw oneself, hold aloof, avoid: 2 Corinthiens 8:20; before ἀπό, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:6 
(cf. ἀπο-, ἐξ-απο-, συν-απο-, δια-, ἐπι-, κατα-, συ(ν)-, ὑπο-στέλλω).†

G4725.def:
στέμμα, -τος, τό
(στέφω, to put around, enwreath) 
a wreath, garland: as used in sacrifices, Actes 14:13.†

G4726.def:
στεναγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(στενάζω), [in LXX for אֲנָחָה, אֲנָקָה, נְאָקָה, etc. ;] 
a groaning: Actes 7:34 (LXX κραυγή), Romains 8:26.†

G4727.def:
στενάζω 
[in LXX for אָנַח ni., אָנַק, etc. ;] 
to groan ("the word denotes feeling which is internal and unexpressed," Mayor, Ja., 162): Marc 7:34, 2 Corinthiens 5:2 5:4, Hébreux 13:17, Jacques 5:9 (EV, murmur); ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, Romains 8:23 (cf. ἀνα-, συ(ν)-στενάζω).†
SYN.: see: κλαίω

G4728.def:
στενός, -ή, -όν 
[in LXX for צַר, etc. ;] 
narrow: fig (v MM, xxiii), Matthieu 7:13-14, Luc 13:24.†

G4729.def:
στενο-χωρέω, -ῶ
(στενός + χῶρος, space) [in LXX: Josué 17:15 (אוּץ), Juges 16:16 (אָלַץ pi.), Ésaïe 28:19 (20) (קָצַר) Ésaïe 49:19 (צָרַר), 4Ma.11:11 * ;] 
__1. to be straitened (cf. Ésaïe 49:19); metaphorically, to be anxious (Hipp., al.). 
__2. In late writers, trans., to straiten, compress (LXX, Diod., al.; π. ap. MM, xxiii): pass., trop., 2 Corinthiens 4:8 6:12.†

G4730.def:
στενοχωρία, -ας, ἡ (see supr.) 
[in LXX for צוֹק, etc. ;] 
narrowness of space, want of room (Thuc., al.). Metaphorical (Ken., Polyb., Deutéronome 28:53, Wis.5:3, al.), difficulty, distress: θλίψις καὶ (ἢ) σ., Romains 2:9 8:35 (EV, anguish); pl. (cf. Bl., § 32, 6; WM, 220), 2 Corinthiens 6:4 12:10.†
SYN.: θλίψις, q.v

G4731.def:
στερεός, -ά, -όν 
[in LXX: Nombres 8:4 (מִקְשָׁה); σ. πέτρα, Ésaïe 5:28 (צַר), etc. ;] 
hard, firm, solid: τροψή, Hébreux 5:12, 14; θεμέλιος, figuratively, 2 Timothée 2:19. Metaphorical, 
__(a) in bad sense, hard, cruel (Hom., al.); 
__(b) in good sense, steadfast, firm: τ. πίστει, 1 Pierre 5:9.†

G4732.def:
στερεόω, -ῶ
(στερεός), [in LXX: Ésaïe 42:5 (רָקַע), Jérémie 5:3 (חָזַק pi.), etc. ;] 
__(a) to make firm or solid; 
__(b) to strengthen, make strong; with accusative of person(s), Actes 3:16; τ. βάσεις, pass., Actes 3:7. Metaphorical (cf. Je, l.with): τ. πίστει, pass., Actes 16:5.†

G4735.def:
στέφανος, -ου, ὁ
(στέφω, to encircle), [in LXX chiefly for עֲטָרָה ;] 
__1. that which surrounds or encompasses (as a wall, a crowd: Hom., al.). 
__2. a crown, i.e. the wreath, garland or chaplet given as a prize for victory, as a festal ornament, or as a public honour for disting­uished service or personal worth (so to sovereigns, especially on the occasion of a παρουσία, which see; cf. Deiss., LAE, 372 ff.; on its use in LXX for the golden crown of royalty (prop., διάδημα, which see, cf. Hort and Mayor on Jacques 1:12): Matthieu 27:29, Marc 15:17, Jean 19:2, 5, 1 Corinthiens 9:25, Apocalypse 4:4, 10 6:2 9:7 12:1 14:14. Metaphorical: Philippiens 4:1, Apocalypse 3:11; τ. δικαιοσύνης (cf. Deiss., LAE, 312), 2 Timothée 4:8; τ. δόξης, 1 Pierre 5:4; καυχήσεως, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:19 (see M, Th., in l); τ. ζωῆς (genitive appos.), Jacques 1:12, Apocalypse 2:10.†

G4737.def:
στεφανόω, -ῶ
(στέφανος), [in LXX for עָטַר ;] 
with accusative of person(s), 
to crown: of a victor, 2 Timothée 2:5. Metaphorical, δόξῃ κ. τιμῇ, Hébreux 2:7, 9" (LXX) .†

G4738.def:
στῆθος, -ους, τό 
[in LXX: Exode 28:23, 26 (29-30) (לֵב), etc. ;] 
the breast: Jean 13:25 21:10, Apocalypse 15:6; as a sign of penitence, τύπτειν (εἰς) τὸ σ., Luc 18:13 23:48,†

G4739.def:
στήκω late Pres., formed from perf., ἕστηκα (see B1., § 17; WH, App., 169; Kennedy, Sources, 158; M, Pr., 238; MM, xxiii), 
[in LXX: Exode 14:13 A, Juges 16:26 B, 3Ki.8:11 B * ;] 
= ἵστημι, to stand: Marc 3:31 11:25, Jean 1:26, Apocalypse 12:4 (ἕστηκεν T). Metaphorical, to stand firm, stand fast: absol., Galates 5:1 (but see Field, Notes, 189 f.), 2 Thessaloniciens 2:15; before ἐν, Jean 8:44 (ἕστηκεν, T, R, mg.), 1 Corinthiens 16:13, Philippiens 1:27 4:1; with dative, Romains 14:4.†

G4740.def:
στηριγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(στηρίζω), [in Sm.: Ésaïe 3:1 * ;] 
__1. a setting firmly, supporting. 
__2. fixedness, firmness, steadfastness: 2 Pierre 3:17.†

G4741.def:
στηρίζω 
[in LXX for סָמַךְ, שׂוּם, etc. ;] 
to fix, set fast, make fast: Luc 16:26; τ. πρόσωτον (Eze.6:2 13:17, al.; see Dalman, Words, 30 f.), Luc 9:51. Metaphorical, to confirm, establish: with, accusative, Luc 22:32, Actes 18:23, Romains 1:11 16:25, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:2 3:13, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:3, Jacques 5:8, 1 Pierre 5:10, Apocalypse 3:2; id. before ἐν, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:17, 2 Pierre 1:12.†

G4742.def:
στίγμα -τος, τό
(στίζω, to prick), [in LXX: Cantique des cantiques 1:11 (נְקֻדָּה) * ;] 
a tattoed mark or brand: τὰ σ. τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, Galates 6:17 (see Lft., in l; Deiss., BS, 349; LAE, 303; MM, xxiii).†

G4743.def:
στιγμή, -ῆς, ἡ
(στίζω, to prick), [in LXX: Ésaïe 29:5 (פֶּתַע), 2Ma.9:11 * ;] 
a prick, a point; metaphorically, σ. χρόνου, a moment: Luc 4:5.†

G4744.def:
στίλβω 
[in LXX: Nahum 3:3 (לַהַב), etc. ;] 
to shine, glisten: Marc 9:3.†

G4745.def:
στοά, -ᾶς, ἡ 
[in LXX: Eze.40:18 (רִצְפָּה), etc. ;] 
a portico: Jean 5:2; used of the covered colonnade in the Temple (EV, porch), Jean 10:23 Actes 3:11 5:12 †

G4746.def:
στοιβάς, see: στιβάς.
στιβάς, -άδος, ἡ, 
[in Aq.: Eze.46:23 (טִירוֺת) * ;] 
a litter of leaves or rushes: pl., Marc 11:8 (Rec. στοιβ-).†

G4747.def:
στοιχεῖον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX: Wis.7:17 19:18, 4Ma.12:13 * ;] 
prop., one of a row (στοῖχος) or series, hence, 
__1. the shadow-line of a dial (Aristoph.). 
__2. an elementary sound or letter of the alphabet (Anth., Plut., π.). 
__3. the elements or rudiments of knowledge (Arist., al.) Hébreux 5:12; πτωχὰ σ., Galates 4:9; σ. τοῦ κόσμου, Galates 4:3, Colossiens 2:8, 20 (but see infr.). 
__4. The material elements of the universe (Plat.; LXX, ll. with): 2 Pierre 3:10 3:12. 
__5. The heavenly bodies (Ding. Laert.). 
__6. The demons or tutelary spirits of nature (Enoch., Test., Sol., al.; for this sense in Ga, Col, ll. with, see ICC on Colossiens 2:8; Enc. Bibl., see word " Elements ").†

G4748.def:
στοιχέω, -ῶ
(στοῖχος, a row), [in LXX: Ecclésiaste 11:6 (כָּשֵׁר) * ;] 
to be in rows (of waves, plants, etc., as well as of men), to walk in line (esp. of marching in file to battle; Xen., Cyr., vi, 3, 34, al.). Metaphorical, in late writers, to walk by rule: Actes 21:24; with dative, to walk by or in (as a rule of life), Romains 4:12 (cf. MM, xxiii), Galates 5:25 6:16, Philippiens 3:16 (cf. συν-στοιχέω).†

G4749.def:
στολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(στέλλω), [in LXX chiefly for בֶּגֶד, also for לְבוּשׁ, etc. ;] 
__1 1, an equipment, an armament (Æsch.). 
__2. Equipment in clothes, apparel, esp. flowing raiment, a festal robe: (cf. Jonas 3:6, Esther 8:15, 1Ma.6:15): Marc 12:38 16:5, Luc 15:22 20:46, Apocalypse 6:11 7:9, 13-14 22:14.†

G4750.def:
στόμα, -τος, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for פֻּם ;] 
the mouth: of man, Matthieu 15:11, Jean 19:29, Actes 11:8, al.; of animals, Matthieu 17:27, 2 Timothée 4:17 (fig.), Hébreux 11:33, Jacques 3:3, al.; figuratively, of inanimate things (ποταμοῦ, Hom.), ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ σ., Apocalypse 12:16; σ. μαχαίρας (Heb. חֶרֶב ־פֶּה, Genèse 34:26 al.), the edge of the sword, Luc 21:24, Hébreux 11:34; esp. of the mouth as the organ of speech: opposite to καρδία, Matthieu 12:34, Romains 10:8, 10; in various phrases (some cl., some resembling Hebrew; cf. Bl., § 40, 9): ἀνοίγειν τ. σ. (see: ἀνοίγω); σ. πρὸς σ. (פֶּה ־אֵל פֶּה Nombres 12:8; = cl., κατὰ σ., Hdt., al.), face to face, II Jn 12, 3Jn.14; διὰ τοῦ σ. (of the Holy Spirit), Luc 1:70, Actes 1:16, al.; ἀπὸ (ἐκ) τοῦ σ. (cf. ἀπὸ σ. εἰπεῖν, Plat., al.), of speaking by word of mouth, Luc 22:71, Actes 22:14; δόλος (ψεῦδος) ἐν τ. σ., 1 Pierre 2:22, Apocalypse 14:5" (LXX) ; metaphorically, ἡ ῥομφαία τοῦ σ., Apocalypse 2:16. By meton., for speech (Soph.): Matthieu 18:16 (LXX), Luc 19:22 21:15, 2 Corinthiens 13:1

G4752.def:
στρατεία (on the orthogr., see Deiss., BS, 181 f.), -ας, ἡ 
(οτρατεύω), [in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;] 
an expedition, a campaign, warfare: metaphorically, 2 Corinthiens 10:4 (-τιά, T), 1 Timothée 1:18.†

G4753.def:
στράτευμα, -τος, τό
(στρατεύω), [in LXX: 1Ma.9:34, 2Ma.5:24 2Mac 8:21 2Mac 12:38 2Mac 13:13; pl., Jdth.11:8, 4Ma.5:1 * ;] 
__1. = στρατεία (Hdt., al.). 
__2. an army, a host: pl., Matthieu 22:7, Apocalypse 9:16 19:14, 19; = soldiers, company of soldiers, Actes 23:10, 27; pl., Luc 23:11.†

G4754.def:
στρατεύω and depon., -ομαι, so always in NT 
(στρατός, an encamped army), [in LXX for מההּ hith., יָצָא, צָבָא; metaphorically, 4Ma.9:23 ;] 
used of the general, to make war, do battle, and (chiefly) of the soldiers serving under him, to serve as a soldier: Luc 3:14, 1 Corinthiens 9:7, 2 Timothée 2:4. Metaphorical (cf. MM, ii, xxiii), of spiritual conflict, to war, make war: 2 Corinthiens 10:3, 1 Timothée 1:18, Jacques 4:1, 1 Pierre 2:11.†

G4755.def:
στρατηγός, -οῦ, ὁ
(στραός, ἄγω), [in LXX chiefly for סָגָן (always in pl.), שַׂר ;] 
__1. a military commander, a general (Hdt., al.). 
__2. A civic commander, a governor, magistrate (Hdt., Xen., al.): Actes 16:20, 22 16:35-36, 38. 
__3. The commander of the Levitical guard of the Temple, ὁ σ. τ. ἱεροῦ (EV, captain of the Temple): Actes 4:1 5:24, 26; pl., Luc 22:4, 52.†
SYN.: ἄρχων (cf. EGT on Actes 16:20; Ramsay, St. Paul, 217).

G4756.def:
στρατιά, -ᾶς, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;] 
__1. = στρατός, an army, a host: of angels (3Ki.22:19, al.), Luc 2:13; of the stars of heaven (Jérémie 8:2, 2 Chroniques 33:3), Actes 7:42. 
__2. As sometimes in cl. (poët.), = στρατεία: 2 Corinthiens 10:4, T (WH, RV, στρατεία).†

G4757.def:
στρατιώτης, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX; 2 Rois 23:8 B1, 2Ma.5:12 2Mac 14:39, III Mac 3:12; 3Ma.3:4 Mac3 * ;] 
a soldier: Matthieu 8:9, Marc 15:16, Jean 19:2, Actes 10:7, al.; metaphorically, σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησ., 2 Timothée 2:3.†

G4758.def:
στρατολογέω, -ῶ
(στρατός, λέγω), 
to levy a troop, enlist soldiers: 2 Timothée 2:4 (Diod., Plut., al.).†

G4759.def:
στρατοπέδ-αρχος (Rec. -ης), -ου, ὁ 
(στρατόπεδον, ἄρχω), a military commander, esp. the Pretorian prefect: Actes 28:16 (WH, om.).† 
στρατοπεδάρχης, see: στρατοπέδαρχος

G4760.def:
στρατό-πεδον, -ου, τό
(στρατός + πέδον, a plain), [in LXX: Jérémie 34:1 (חַיִל), 2Ma.8:12, al. ;] 
__(a) a military camp; 
__(b) an army: Luc 21:20.†

G4761.def:
στρεβλόω, -ῶ
(στρέφω), [in LXX: 2 Rois 22:27 (פָּתַל hithp.), 3Ma.4:14, 4Ma.9:17 4Mac 12:4 4Mac 12:11 4Mac 15:14 * ;] 
to twist, torture. Metaphorical (cf. 2Ki, l.with), to twist or pervert language: 2 Pierre 3:16.†

G4762.def:
στρέφω 
[in LXX chiefly for הָפַךְ, also for סָבַב, etc. ;] 
to turn: with accusative of thing(s) dative of person(s), Matthieu 5:39; = ἀποσ-, to bring back, Matthieu 27:3 (cf. Ésaïe 38:8); reflexively (WM, § 38, 1), to turn oneself, Actes 7:42; with accusative before εἰς, = μετασ-, to change, Apocalypse 11:6. Pass., reflexive, to turn oneself: before εἰς, Jean 20:14, Actes 7:39 13:46; ptcp., στραφείς, with indic., Matthieu 7:6 9:22 16:23, Luc 7:9 9:55 14:25 22:61, Jean 1:38 20:16; id. before πρός, Luc 7:44 10:22 (WH, R, om.), Luc 7:23 23:28; metaphorically, to change: absol., Matthieu 18:3, Jean 12:40 (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ, ἐπι-, κατα-, μετα-, συ(ν)-, ὑπο-στρέφω).†

G4763.def:
στρηνιάω, ῶ
(στρῆνος, which see), [in Sm.: Ésaïe 61:6 (אָכַל) * ;] 
a word which first appears in the middle comedy (Rutherford, NPhr., 475 f.), to run riot, wax wanton: Apocalypse 18:7-9 (cf. κατα-στρηνιάω).†
SYN.: σπαταλάω (which see), τρυφάω

G4764.def:
στρῆνος, -ους, τό
(cf. Lat. strenuus), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:28 (שַׁאֲנָן)* ;] 
insolent luxury, wantonness: Apocalypse 18:3 (a late word, first found in a Comic poet, B.C. 300, see Kennedy, Sources, 41, cf. στρηνιάω).†

G4765.def:
στρουθίον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for צִפּוֹר ;] 
dimin. of στρουθός 
a sparrow: Matthieu 10:29, 31, Luc 12:6-7.†

G4766.def:
στρωννύω or στρώννυμι
(seeBl., § 23, 1; Veitch, see word), [in LXX for יַצַע hoph., etc. ;] 
to spread: ἱμάτια ἐν τ. ὁδῷ (εἰς τ. ὁδόν), Matthieu 21:8, Marc 11:8; of making a bed, στρῶσον (sc. τ. κλίνην) σεαυτῷ, Actes 9:34; of furnishing a room, ἐστρωμένον, spread with carpets or carpeted couches (cf. Eze.23:41), Marc 14:15, Luc 22:12.†

G4767.def:
στυγητός, -όν
(στυγέω, to hate), 
hated, hateful: Tite 3:3.†

G4768.def:
στυγνάζω
(στυγνός, sombre, gloomy, sullen, Ésaïe 5:17, Wis.17:5, Dan LXX 2:12*), [in LXX: Eze.27:35 28:19 32:10 (שָׁמֵם)* ;] 
to have a sombre, gloomy appearance: of the human countenance (RV, his countenance fell), Marc 10:22; of the sky (so στυγνότης, Polyb., iv, 21, 1), Matthieu 16:3 ([WH], R, mg., om.).†

G4769.def:
στύλος (T, στῦλος, as in cl.), -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for עַמּוּד, also for קֶרֶשׁ, etc. ;] 
a pillar, regarded especially as a support: σ. πυρός, Apocalypse 10:1; σ. ἐν τ. ναῷ, figuratively, Apocalypse 3:12, Metaphorical, Galates 2:9; τ. ἀληθείας, 1 Timothée 3:15.†

G4771.def:
σύ, 
pron. of 2nd of person(s), 
thou, you, genitive, σοῦ, dative, σοί, accusative, σέ, pl., ὑμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς (enclitic in oblique cases sing., except after prep. (BL, §48, 3), though πρὸς σέ occurs in Matthieu 25:39). Nom. for emphasis or contrast: Jean 1:30, 4:10, 5:33, 39, 44, Actes 4:7, Éphésiens 5:32; so also perhaps σὺ εἶπας, Matthieu 26:64, al. (M, Pr., 86); before voc., Matthieu 2:6, Luc 1:76, Jean 17:5, al.; sometimes without emphasis (M, Pr., 85f.), as also in cl., but esp. as rendering of Heb. phrase, e.g. υἱός μου εἶ σύ (בְּנִי־אַתָּה, Psaumes 2:7), Actes 13:33. The genitive (σοῦ, ὑμῶν) is sometimes placed bef. the noun: Luc 7:48, 12:30, al.; so also the enclitic σοῦ, Matthieu 9:6; on τί ἐμοὶ κ. σοί, see: ἐγώ.

G4772.def:
συγγένεια, -ας, ἡ
(συγγενής), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁפָּחָה ;] 
__1. kinship. 
__2. By meton., kinsfolk, kindred: Luc 1:61, Actes 7:3, 14 †

G4773.def:
σνγγενής, -ές (dative pl., -εῦσιν, Marc 6:4, Luc 2:44, as though from -εύς, see Swete, Mk., l.with; Bl., § 8, 6; cf. 1Ma.10:89 A א2 *;) 
(σύν, γένος), [in LXX for דּוֹד, דּוֹדָה, מִשְׁפָּחָה ;] 
__1. congenital, natural, innate. 
__2. akin to; as subst., a kinsman: Marc 6:4, Luc 1:58 2:44 14:12 21:16, Jean 18:26, Actes 10:24; of tribal kinship, Romains 9:3 16:7, 11 16:21.†
SYN.: ἴδιος, οἰκεῖος (which see)

G4774.def:
συν-γνώμη (Rec. συγγ-), -ης, ἡ
(συγγιγνώσκω, (a) to agree with; (b) to pardon), [in LXX: Sir prol.14 (B1N1 cm.) 313, 2Mac 14:20* ;] 
__1. confession. 
__2. fellow feeling; hence, concession, allowance: 1 Corinthiens 7:6 (see ICC, in l). 
__3. pardon.†

G4775.def:
συν-κάθημαι
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Psaumes 101:6 (יָשַׁב) * ;] 
to sit together or with: with dative, Actes 26:30; before μετά, with genitive, Marc 14:54.†

G4776.def:
περι-καθ-ίζω 
[in LXX for חָנָה, לָחַם ni., etc. ;] 
__1. to invest, besiege (Diod., 4Ki.6:24, 1Ma.11:61, al.). 
__2. to sit around: Luc 22:55, L, txt.
†

G4777.def:
συν-κακοπαθέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, 
to bear evil treatment along with, take one's share of ill-treatment: 2 Timothée 2:3; with dative commod., τ. εὐαγγελίῳ, 2 Timothée 2:18.†

G4778.def:
συν-κακουχέομαι (Rec. συγκ-), -οῦμαι, pass. 
to endure adversity with: with dative of person(s), Hébreux 11:25. Not elsewhere.†

G4779.def:
συν-καλέω
(Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, [in LXX for קָרָא ;] 
to call together: with accusative, Marc 15:16, Luc 15:6, 9 (seel. -εῖται, see B1., § 55, 1), Actes 5:21. Mid., to call together to oneself: Luc 9:1 (and seel. in Luc 15:6, 9 see supr.) Luc 23:13, Actes 10:24 28:17.†

G4780.def:
συν-καλύπτω
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX chiefly for כָּסָה pi. ;] 
to veil or cover completely: with accusative, pass., Luc 12:2.†

G4781.def:
συν-κάμπτω
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Psaumes 68:10, 23 (מעד hi.), etc. ;] 
to bend completely, bend together: τ. νῶτον, figuratively, Romains 11:10 (LXX).†

G4782.def:
συν-κατα-βαίνω
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Psaumes 49:17 (יָרַד), Wis.10:13, Dan LXX TH 3:49 * ;] 
to go down with: Actes 25:5. In late writers also metaphorically (Wis, l.with), to condescend, on WH. see Rutherford, NPhr., 485 f.†

G4783.def:
συν-κατά-θεσις (Rec συγκ-), -εως, ἡ
(συνκατατίθημι) 
concord, agreement: 2 Corinthiens 6:16 (Polyb., Plut., al.).†

G4784.def:
συν-κατα-τίθημι
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Exode 23:1 (שִׁית יָד), Exode 23:32 (בְּרִית), Da TH Su 1:20 * ;] 
to deposit together. Mid., to deposit one's vote with, hence, to agree with, assent to: with dative, Luc 23:51.†

G4785.def:
συν-κατα-ψηφίζω (Rec. συγκ-), 
__1. to condemn with or together (Plut., Themist., 21). 
__2. to vote one a place among: pass., Actes 1:26. Not elsewhere .†

G4786.def:
συν-κεράννυμι
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Dan LXX 2:43 (עֲרַב ithpa.), 2Ma.15:39 * ;] 
to mix or blend together, compound: with accusative, 1 Corinthiens 12:24; ptcp. pf. pass., Hébreux 4:2, T, WH, mg., R, mg.; id., of persons, with dative instr., to be united with, agree with, ib., WH, txt., R, txt. (see Westc., in l).†

G4787.def:
συν-κινέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, 
to move together. Metaphorical, to excite, stir up: τ. λαόν, Actes 6:12 (Arist., Polyb., al.).†

G4788.def:
συν-κλείω
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX chiefly for סגר ;] 
to shut together, enclose, shut in on all sides: of a catch of fish, Luc 5:6; metaphorically (Psaumes 31:9, al.), Romains 11:32, Galates 3:22-23.†

G4789.def:
συν-κληρο-νόμος (Rec. συγκ-), -ου, ὁ 
a co-inheritor, fellow-heir: Romains 8:17, Éphésiens 3:6; with genitive of thing(s), Hébreux 11:9, 1 Pierre 3:7 (for exx., see Deiss., LAE, 88 f.).†

G4790.def:
συν-κοινωνέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, 
to have fellowship with or in (in cl., with genitive of thing(s), dative of person(s)): with dative of thing(s), Éphésiens 5:11, Apocalypse 18:4; id. with genitive of person(s), Philippiens 4:14.†

G4791.def:
συν-κοινωνός (Rec. συγκ-), όν, 
partaking jointly of: with genitive of thing(s), Romains 11:17, 1 Corinthiens 9:23; id. with genitive of person(s), Philippiens 1:7; before ἐν, Apocalypse 1:9.†

G4792.def:
συν-κομίζω
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Job 5:26 (עָלָה) * ;] 
__1. to bring together, collect (Hdt., Xen., al.). 
__2. to take up a body for burial (Soph., Aj., 1048): Actes 8:2 (see Field, Notes, 116).†

G4793.def:
συν-κρίνω (Rec. συγκ-) 
[in LXX chiefly for פָּתַר ;] 
__1. to compound, combine: 1 Corinthiens 2:13, R, mg.1 (Lft., Notes, 180 f.). 
__2. In Arist. and later writers (Wis.7:29, a1.) = παραβάλλω, to compare: 1Co, l.with, R, txt. (Field, Notes, 168), 2 Corinthiens 10:12 
__3. In LXX, of dreams, to interpret (Genèse 40:8, 1Co, l.with, R, mg. 2 (but see reff. supr.).†

G4794.def:
συν-κύπτω
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Job 9:27 (עָזַב), Sir.12:11 19:26 * ;] 
__1. to bend forwards (Arist., al.). 
__2. to be bowed down: Luc 13:11.†

G4795.def:
συγκυρία, -ας, ἡ
(συγκυρέω, to happen), [in Sm.: 1 Rois 6:9 (מִקְרֶה) * ;] (more frequently in late writers, συγκύρησις, -ημα), 
chance, coincidence: κατὰ σ. (see MM, xxiii), Luc 10:31 (Hippocr., Eccl.).†

G4796.def:
συν-χαίρω
(Rec. συγ-), [in LXX: Genèse 21:6 (צָחַק), 3Ma.1:8 R * ;] 
__1. to rejoice with: with dative of person(s), Luc 1:58 15:6, 9, Philippiens 2:17-18, EV; with dative of thing(s), 1 Corinthiens 12:26 13:6. 
__2. to congratulate (Æschin., Polyb., al.): Phi, l.with (Lft., in I.; cf. MM, xxiv).†

G4797.def:
συν-χέω
(Rec. συγ-), [in LXX for בָּלַל, רָגַז, etc. ;] 
to pour together, commingle, confuse; metaphorically, confound, throw into confusion, stir up trouble: Actes 21:27 (cf. συν-χύννω).†

G4798.def:
συν-χράομαι
(Rec. συγ-), -ῶμαι, [in Al.: 1 Rois 30:19 * ;] 
to use together with. Metaphorical, with dative of person(s), to associate with: Jean 4:9 (Polyb., a1.).†

G4799.def:
σύγχυσις, -εως, ἡ
(συγχέω), [in LXX: Genèse 11:9 (בָּבֶל), 1 Rois 5:6 5:12(11) 1 Rois 14:20 (מְהוּמָה) * ;] 
confusion: of a popular uproar, Actes 19:29.†
